nodes.description: There is no treatment for the ciliary defect. The proband's chronic airway disease and bronchiectasis are managed with the supportive care used across primary ciliary dyskinesia: airway clearance, prompt treatment of infections, and surveillance of lung function. Nothing in it is DNAH1-specific.

nodes.description: Weak ciliary beating fails to move mucus out of the nose, sinuses, middle ear and bronchi. Retained secretions lead to chronic rhinitis, cough and bronchitis, and repeated infection damages the bronchial wall into bronchiectasis. This is the general PCD mechanism; it has not been measured in CILD37 patients.

nodes.description: Loss of an inner-arm heavy chain weakens and distorts the ciliary beat. In Dnah1 knockout mice the tracheal ciliary beat frequency falls by about half without any gross change in axonemal structure, which is why such a defect can be missed by electron microscopy. Respiratory cilia of CILD37 patients have not been examined, so this node rests on mouse data and on the location of DNAH1 in human respiratory cilia.
